# Requirements

- [-] **[MUST]** Reproducible training
  - Criteria: Same seed produces same loss curve within 1%

- [ ] **[MUST]** Canonical multi-session retrieve-skills service

Any capability that a harness cannot enforce natively MUST be identified as advisory and tested as advisory rather than claimed equivalent.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Prevent and measure artifact sprawl
  - Criteria: Before and after every non-trivial change, the harness MUST inventory newly created or modified files, configuration entries, modules, classes, functions/methods, and persisted records; record the incumbent-search result and parent intent/spec/task for each new artifact; and detect untracked, duplicate, superseded, unreferenced, over-complex, and unreachable artifacts. Every production code symbol MUST be reachable from a declared root (public API, executable entry point, hook, callback, plugin registration, framework route, scheduled job, or another reachable symbol). A deliberately inactive symbol MUST carry a machine-readable pending marker linked to an active SpecsDB task and remain outside production roots; a completed, dropped, deprecated, or missing task makes that symbol orphaned. Function/class size and complexity measurements are leading indicators that trigger review; orphan status is determined by reachability and traceability. Completion requires orphan-count delta <= 0, no unexplained unreachable symbols, and at least three varied fixtures with durable census and call-graph evidence.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Measure trajectory decoherence against approved intent
  - Criteria: At implementation start, the harness MUST snapshot the approved intent, requirements, decisions, and task scope as the reference trajectory. Convergence MUST inspect the implementation and evidence for every acceptance criterion, then report semantic drift (unmet or unlinked criteria), coordination drift (unresolved contradictions among active agents/artifacts), and behavioral drift (actions or strategies outside approved scope/gates) separately. Each drift count MUST be zero for convergence; checkbox completion alone MUST NOT produce CONVERGED; gaps and evidence MUST persist through SpecsDB.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Block mutable-growing-Karp through anomaly evidence

An explanation, health signal, or zero process exit code alone MUST NOT close the anomaly. Conformance MUST cover at least three varied cases, including a healthy server with a failed registered client session.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Measure code health without confusing complexity with sprawl
  - Criteria: The harness MUST compute differential code-health metrics for changed code and trend them by module: logical lines per function/method, public methods per class, class and module size, cyclomatic/cognitive complexity, nesting depth, fan-in/fan-out, duplicate blocks, unused imports, unreachable symbols, and architecture-boundary violations. Reachability, traceability, duplication, and boundary violations are hard gates; size and complexity are warning signals calibrated from the repository baseline and reviewed when they regress. Initial tool selection MUST prefer a minimal pinned set that covers lint, dead-code analysis, complexity, duplication, dependency boundaries, and dynamic coverage; overlapping scanners MUST be collapsed. Threshold changes MUST carry provenance and a before/after false-positive evaluation.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Bound control-flow complexity and routing indirection
  - Criteria: For every changed critical path, the harness MUST build a control-flow and call-path graph from each declared entry root to observable outcomes and failure exits. It MUST report: maximum conditional nesting, cyclomatic and cognitive complexity, branch fan-out, duplicated predicates, routing-only hops, pass-through hops, class/module boundary crossings, repeated boundary crossings, cycles, and maximum root-to-outcome path length. More than 3 consecutive routing-only or pass-through hops, nesting deeper than 4, repeated A→B→A boundary ping-pong, an unexplained cycle, or duplicated branching policy MUST trigger review. These are structural warnings unless they violate an architecture boundary or create unreachable behavior, which are hard failures. Refactoring guidance MUST prefer guard clauses for preconditions, decision tables or match/switch for closed homogeneous variants, and Strategy/State/polymorphism only when the same behavior axis recurs; a clear two-branch conditional MUST NOT be abstracted merely to reduce counts. Runtime-efficiency claims MUST be backed by profiler or benchmark evidence rather than static hop counts.

The gate runner MUST persist the invocation and evidence before returning its aggregate verdict. Analyzers MUST be read-only fact producers; renderers and harness adapters MUST be projections at the edges. Tasks MUST remain execution state and MUST NOT silently become policy. - [ ] **[MUST]** Automate conversation-to-durable-memory promotion via one global store
  - Criteria: The memory-index service MUST maintain ONE global append-only conversation store that all five harnesses write to via MCP. Every volley MUST be tagged with harness ID, project slug, canonical session ID, sequence number, timestamp, role, and provider metadata hash. The hot window is a client-side view: the 13 most recent volleys for the current (harness, project) cross-section, served by a single query. Everything older than the hot window MUST be retrievable via RAG with Ebbinghaus recency-weighted decay. Retrieval count MUST be tracked per observation; observations reaching 3 retrievals MUST auto-promote into durable markdown (repo memory-bank for project-specific, global memory-bank for cross-project) without a manual agent call. Promotion MUST classify candidates and route to the correct lane: memory-bank markdown for facts/decisions, SpecsDB proposal for requirements/decisions/tasks, steering proposal for policy/constraints, or skill candidate for recurring procedures. Promoted artifacts MUST retain provenance links to source volley IDs and retrieval timestamps. Observations below the retrieval threshold MUST decay via configurable stability/half-life and become dormant without deletion. A Kiro session on project X MUST be able to recall what a Claude Code session on project X previously surfaced via the same RAG tier, because the project dimension—not the harness—is the primary filter for relevance.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Provide one idempotent setup command that converges from any starting state
  - Criteria: The harness MUST provide one idempotent setup command that detects current state (which services are running, which configs exist, which harnesses are installed), skips anything already in place, and only acts on the delta. Setup MUST cover: skill store presence, service health per port, MCP registration per harness, steering projection per harness, conversation store schema, and supervisor status. Re-running setup after a successful run MUST produce zero changes and exit cleanly. Setup MUST report what it checked, what it skipped, and what it changed. A fresh machine with prerequisites installed MUST reach full operational state in one invocation.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Enforce phased execution with parallel batching and 4-phase script cap
  - Criteria: Every implementation plan MUST decompose into dependency phases before execution begins. Independent tasks within a phase MUST execute in parallel. Phase transitions MUST gate on verification of all prior-phase outputs. Each phase MUST declare an artifact manifest (files created, state changes, verification results) that is written to disk before the phase is declared complete. No single script may exceed 4 phases (node complexity cap). The critical path through any pipeline (longest chain of sequential dependencies) MUST NOT exceed 7 (depth cap). Width (parallel work within a phase) is unbounded. Each node MUST be independently re-runnable from its declared disk inputs without re-running prior nodes. Pipelines whose critical path would exceed 7 MUST decompose into independent sub-pipelines that share artifacts on disk rather than forming one causal chain. A crash between phases MUST lose zero work. A new session MUST resume from the last completed phase checkpoint without re-running prior phases.

  - Criteria: When a spec defines N axes of stratification (e.g. regime x dataset x answer_type), implementation MUST sample across ALL N axes independently. Collapsing any axis into a domain=ALL shortcut violates the spec even if volume coverage appears adequate. The gate MUST block any implementation that reduces dimensionality below what the spec requires. Verification: every cell in the cross-product grid must be explicitly constructed, not reached by accident of volume.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Scene-drafting agent: bible + rolling window → narrative manuscript
  - Criteria: Given a generated adventure module (.md bible), produce a coherent narrative manuscript by drafting scenes sequentially through a rolling context window. Each scene must reference only facts established in the bible or prior scenes. No hallucinated details that contradict the bible.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Rolling window composition: bible excerpt + recent scenes + contracts
  - Criteria: The rolling window must contain: (1) the current room entry from the bible, (2) monster behavior contracts for creatures in that room, (3) the last 2-3 generated scenes for continuity, (4) party state if tracked. Total context per generation call must fit within 8192 output tokens.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Prose generation via muse-glimmer-30b (scene tier)
  - Criteria: Use meta/muse-glimmer-30b for scene prose generation (creative tier). The bible/structure is already produced by nemotron. Scene generation is a prose-only task — no JSON, no structured output needed.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Output: single manuscript .md file with ordered scenes
  - Criteria: Output is a single markdown file — the manuscript — with scenes in traversal order. Each scene is headed by the room name. The bible .md is the input, the manuscript .md is the output.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Per-scene coherence gate via nemotron before window slides
  - Criteria: After each scene is generated, feed it to nemotron (planner tier) with the room brief and ask: "Does this scene contain physical impossibilities, spatial contradictions, or logical breaks between consecutive sentences? List them." If issues found, regenerate the scene with the feedback. Max 2 retries per scene.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Final editorial sweep: full-manuscript coherence check post-draft
  - Criteria: After all scenes are drafted, run a final editorial pass over the full manuscript using nemotron. Flag: (1) physical/spatial impossibilities, (2) continuity breaks between scenes, (3) characters doing things that contradict their established situation. Output a list of issues with scene + line references. Regenerate flagged scenes with the issues as feedback.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Adversarial convergence: two models critique each other per scene
  - Criteria: Each scene is produced by a two-model loop: (1) Writer A (muse-glimmer-30b) drafts, (2) Writer B (minimax-m3) identifies weak/incoherent lines and rewrites them, (3) Writer A reviews B's rewrite — accepts changes it agrees with, rejects ones that damage voice/meaning, (4) if disagreements remain, one more round. Max 3 rounds. Output is the consensus version. Both models must agree on the final text or the best version after 3 rounds is accepted.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Writer B critique format: identify + rewrite, not just flag
  - Criteria: Writer B's critique must identify: (1) synesthetic metaphors (materials performing actions they physically cannot), (2) logical/spatial incoherence between consecutive sentences, (3) purple filler (sentences that advance nothing). For each flagged line, B provides a rewrite — not just a flag. The output is the full scene with B's rewrites inline.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Writer A review: per-change accept/reject with merged output
  - Criteria: Writer A's review of B's rewrite accepts or rejects each change individually. Acceptance criterion: the rewrite preserves narrative meaning and improves physical specificity. Rejection criterion: the rewrite damages voice, removes necessary information, or introduces its own tics. Output: the merged scene with accepted changes applied.

- [ ] **[MUST]** Convergence bound: max 3 rounds, early exit on agreement
  - Criteria: The convergence loop is bounded at 3 rounds maximum. If convergence (zero rejected changes) is reached earlier, stop. If after 3 rounds there are still disagreements, take the version with fewer flagged issues. Log round count per scene to stderr.

- [ ] **[SHOULD]** Parse adventure module markdown automatically
  - Criteria: The agent must parse the existing adventure_module_*.md format to extract room order, room descriptions, monster roster, and behavior contracts. No manual pre-processing required.
